newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Views split on Belgian linear bonds future.
newsitem.headline: Views split on Belgian linear bonds future.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds, which outperformed Bunds on Tuesday, could go either way in coming days depending on whether, or buy how much, the U.S. Federal Reserve raises rates later in the day, traders said.

"If the Fed does nothing or raises rates by just 25 points it could pressure the dollar and with it the non-mark currencies such as the French and Belgian francs," one trader said. "This in turn could lead to a widening of the bond spread over Bunds."
However, Generale Bank sees the spread possibly narrowing to just 10 basis points, according to an article in the Financieel Economische Tijd newspaper.
But traders reported strong selling emerging when the 10-year spread over Bunds narrowed to 17 basis points.

The benchmark 2006 OLO ended the day yielding 6.34 percent against Monday's closing 6.39, and the spread over Bunds was 18 basis points against Monday's closing 20, after having touched 17 at one stage on Tuesday.

Traders said there was a lot of buying in the morning around the middle of the maturity range, 2003 to 2005, partly on follow-through from Monday's auction of the March 2007 OLO and partly on one big new buy order.
However, this evaporated in the afternoon, they said.
The front month futures contract finished Tuesday 45 basis points or 0.38 percent higher at 118.82, having moved in a 118.94/118.39 range.
